concept: Orphaned documents and read concern available versus local
summary: Source-anchored research for Orphaned documents and read concern available versus local. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Available is not a reliable exhaustive orphan inventory by itself: SERVER-69219 records that shard-key predicates can target only a subset of shards and thereby miss unowned documents on other shards. The ticket's 2023 resolution rejected changing all such reads to broadcasts. (low confidence)

For covered queries issued through mongos on sharded collections, MongoDB documents that the index must contain the shard key. Historical SERVER-8405 explains the ownership-check problem that motivates index-based chunk membership checks when the shard key is present. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-8405

Do not use an apparently covered execution path as proof of correct orphan filtering: SERVER-14304 records an _id equality/projection optimization that bypassed the sharding filter and returned incorrect or duplicated results in MongoDB 2.6.0–2.6.2; the recorded fix shipped in 2.6.3. This is historical evidence, not a claim that modern releases retain that bug. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents that an index covering a sharded query through mongos must include the shard key, and that all fields in the query, including those needed internally for sharding, must be part of an index. Separately, read concern available does not check that the correct shard received the query and can return orphaned documents during chunk migration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md

For unsharded collections, including standalone and replica-set deployments, local and available behave identically. The shard-ownership tradeoff therefore must not be generalized to every MongoDB read. (high confidence)

Huawei Cloud describes orphaned documents as documents remaining on one shard while their chunks exist on another shard, including after failed migrations or incomplete migration cleanup following an abnormal shutdown. (medium confidence)

For sharded collections, read concern available does not require confirmation that the receiving shard is the authoritative owner. During a partition involving chunk migration, it can return orphaned documents and incorrect or unexpected results. This is a possibility, not a guarantee that every available read returns orphans. (high confidence)

Huawei Cloud's procedure for checking orphaned documents runs db.getSiblingDB("dbName").collName.find().readPref("secondary").readConcern("local").explain("executionStats") through mongos and reads chunkSkips in the SHARDING_FILTER stage, which it describes as the number of orphaned documents on the current shard for the collection checked. Alibaba Cloud's ApsaraDB for MongoDB documentation describes a similar method, using a plain find().explain("executionStats") on each shard and checking whether the SHARDING_FILTER chunkSkips field is not 0. Alibaba's version does not specify readPref or readConcern, and its page does not scope the check to MongoDB 5.0 and earlier. Sources: https://support.huaweicloud.com/intl/en-us/drs_faq/drs_09_0101.html ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dts/support/how-do-you-clean-up-orphaned-documents-in-a-mongodb-sharded-cluster

Available and local behave identically for unsharded collections; available does not guarantee majority persistence, so choosing local for ownership filtering must not be confused with obtaining majority durability. (medium confidence)

MongoDB documents read concern local as an alternative that avoids the risk of returning orphaned documents when reading from sharded collections. Read concern available does not require a check that the correct shard received the query, and can return orphaned documents if the shard was undergoing chunk migration. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md

Avoiding orphaned results with local does not establish majority durability: both local and available can return data that has not reached a majority of replica-set members and may subsequently roll back. (high confidence)

Huawei Cloud and Alibaba Cloud document a diagnostic through mongos using find().readPref("secondary").readConcern("local").explain("executionStats") and inspecting SHARDING_FILTER.chunkSkips for orphaned records rejected on each shard. Alibaba scopes this particular method to MongoDB 5.0 or earlier instances. Both warn that the unfiltered diagnostic scans documents across shards, so its cost can be substantial. Treat it as their documented diagnostic, not a universal explain-output contract for every server version. (medium confidence) Sources: https://support.huaweicloud.com/intl/en-us/drs_faq/drs_09_0101.html ; https://help.aliyun.com/zh/mongodb/support/how-to-clean-up-orphaned-documents

Ownership filtering and physical cleanup are separate operations: the local-read explain diagnostic reports orphaned documents that exist on a shard (via chunkSkips), and both Huawei Cloud and Alibaba Cloud describe a separate cleanupOrphaned procedure to remove them. Sources: https://support.huaweicloud.com/intl/en-us/drs_faq/drs_09_0101.html ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dts/support/how-do-you-clean-up-orphaned-documents-in-a-mongodb-sharded-cluster
